title: The Delayed Upgrade Penalty ratchets upward on a fixed schedule to force MKR conversion without a deadline
content:
A.4.1.2.1.1.1 gives holders a standing right to convert MKR to SKY at a fixed 1:24,000 rate, "subject to the Delayed Upgrade Penalty." A.4.1.2.1.1.1.1 defines the penalty's trajectory: set to 1% in the September 18, 2025 Executive Vote, and "increased gradually at the rate of 1 percentage point per 3 months thereafter."

The mechanism design is the claim, not the numbers. A migration deadline creates a cliff: everything is fine until a date, after which value is destroyed outright and anyone who missed it has a grievance. A monotonically rising penalty instead makes delay continuously costly while never removing the option. Holders self-select their exit time against their own cost of acting, and the protocol never has to choose between stranding balances and supporting a legacy token forever.

Because the schedule is *pre-announced and open-ended*, it is also credible. Nobody needs to trust future governance to raise the penalty; the ruleset already says it rises, so waiting for leniency is not a rational strategy. The escalation eventually approaches confiscatory levels, which is how a soft mechanism achieves a hard deadline's effect without a hard deadline's discontinuity.

The cost is a slow-burning obligation: the penalty must keep being applied, and its indefinite ramp means the Atlas carries a live parameter that will look absurd if the migration is ever declared complete.
description: Rising 1 percentage point every 3 months indefinitely, it replaces a cliff deadline with continuous pressure: converting is always possible, but always more expensive than yesterday.
